newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes slumber through UK bank holiday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes slumber through UK bank holiday.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices slumbered through a UK bank holiday Monday afternoon, although technicals fueled a bounce in the outright price of West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, traders said.
June WTI/Cushing was trading around $19.70-80 a barrel, up some 15 cents from late Friday's cash market.
July WTI/Cushing was running around three cents ahead of the June level.
"(The market's) a real sleeper," a Houston trader said. "With Brent closed, it makes it hard to see where the arbitrage is."

Among the grades, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was talked slightly weaker at June WTI/Cushing minus five to three cents, with minus four cents last changing hands, traders said. The grade last traded at flat late Friday.
WTI/Midland was at a steady 32-30 cents under WTI/Cushing, with minus 31 last traded.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire hovered around minus 45-40 cents a barrel.
West Texas Sour/Midland was around minus $1.72-70, while Eugene Island was steady at a discount of around $1.50-45. Eugene was last done at minus $1.50 on Friday.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus was stable at $1.80-84 a barrel.
